title: The holy bond
hookLine: all things are woven together, and the bond is holy (Meditations 7.9)

cards: Back in year one, sympatheia came up: the Stoic idea that everything touches everything, and the cup in your hand traced back to the people who made it.
In book seven, Marcus says it again, but he adds one word that changes the temperature. Connected is a fact, like plumbing. Marcus doesn't stop at connected.
He calls the connection holy. That's a different kind of claim, and it asks something different of you.

teach.b: Meditations seven, nine, in George Long's translation: "All things are implicated with one another, and the bond is holy." In Long's English, implicated means entangled, wound in together, like threads in cloth.
Hardly anything, Marcus adds, is foreign to anything else.

teach.h: ONE UNIVERSE, ONE LAW, ONE REASON.
teach.b: Then the passage builds like a creed: one universe made of everything, one God running through everything, one substance, one law, one reason shared by every thinking creature, one truth.
However a listener thinks about God, notice what Marcus is doing. He isn't describing a machine; he's describing something he reveres. When something is holy, you don't just know about it.
You handle it with care, and you don't break it for convenience.
So if the bond between you and others is holy, then cutting someone off out of spite, cheating a stranger you'll never see again, or talking about someone as if they were nothing isn't just unkind.
For Marcus it's a kind of sacrilege, a tearing of something sacred.
Other paths have their own language for sacred ties, such as covenant, communion or dependent arising, and each explains its own in its own way. This lesson borrows none of them.
Holy here is Marcus's Stoic word: a living cosmos with reason running through it, and a bond he thinks is worth revering.

how: Readers of Marcus sometimes use 7.9 as a reminder that their ties to other people are not only practical but worth treating with reverence, especially toward strangers they'll never see again.

games.q: you'll never see this stranger again, and cutting a corner on them would cost you nothing. by 7.9, what's at stake?
o: nothing, since you won't meet again.
games.why: Meditations 7.9: all things are bound together, the bond is holy, and hardly anything is foreign to anything else.

practice: Bring to mind one person you're tied to in a way you rarely notice: the neighbor whose name you know, a cousin far away, the person who drives your bus.
Trace one thread between you, what they've given you, what you've given them, what you share. Hold that thread gently, the way you'd hold something sacred.
